subject: Economics
description: GDP, GNP, NNP, NDP, per capita income

questions.explanation: GDP — Gross Domestic Product — market value of all final goods and services produced WITHIN a country's borders in a year. GNP includes NET factor income from abroad (GNP = GDP + NFIA).
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: The relationship between GDP and GNP is:

options.option_text: GNP = GDP + NFIA (Net Factor Income from Abroad)

questions.explanation: GNP = GDP + NFIA. NFIA = income from abroad by citizens − income paid to foreigners for their work/investments here. For India, NFIA is typically NEGATIVE (more repatriated out than brought in), so GNP < GDP. NDP = GDP − depreciation. NNP = GNP − depreciation.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: PER CAPITA INCOME is calculated as:
questions.explanation: Per capita income = National Income (or GDP) / Population. Useful indicator of individual prosperity; but hides inequality. India's per capita income (2024): around $2,500-2,700 (nominal). Much higher in PPP terms.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: India's National Accounts / National Income estimates are published by:
questions.explanation: NSO — under MoSPI (Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation). Combines the former CSO (Central Statistics Office) + NSSO. Base year of GDP series: 2011-12 currently; 2022-23 series under development. Quarterly GDP released ~2 months after quarter end.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: REAL GDP vs NOMINAL GDP: the difference is:

options.option_text: Real GDP includes inflation effects; nominal does not
Nominal GDP is at current prices; Real GDP is adjusted for inflation (at constant/base-year prices)

questions.explanation: Nominal GDP — in current prices (inflated). Real GDP — deflated using a GDP deflator or base year prices, reflects actual output change. Real growth is the more meaningful measure of economic expansion.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: India is the world's ___ LARGEST economy (nominal GDP, 2024-25):
questions.explanation: India surpassed UK in nominal GDP ~2022 to become 5th largest economy (~$3.9 trillion as of 2024; projected to pass Germany/Japan by 2026-27 → 3rd largest). By PPP, India is already 3rd largest (after China and USA).
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: 'PPP' (Purchasing Power Parity) adjustment is used to:

options.option_text: Compare national incomes by adjusting for cost-of-living differences

questions.explanation: PPP — equalises the purchasing power of different currencies by comparing what a basket of goods costs in each country. Famous 'Big Mac Index' (Economist magazine). India's GDP is much larger in PPP terms than in nominal USD because costs are lower.
